correctness.rationale: For two-row ladder L_n and K=Cliq_4(L_n) (faces with no independent 4-set), published total 4-cut ladder wedge theorem and combinatorial Alexander duality establish that reduced rational homology concentrates in H5 with dimension N=binom(n−1,3). For a row-swap or reflection involution g, reduced Lefschetz identifies trace on H5 with sum over invariant faces of (−1)^(number of length2 vertex orbits + fixed singleton orbits). A rung-orbit subset of size t has independence number t, giving tr(row swap)=Σ_(t=0)^3 (−1)^t C(n,t)=−N. Even/odd column reflection and combined reflection reduce to eligible 1-,2-,3-pair-orbit unions; bipartite matching (König) restricts all faces to size≤6 and yields tr(column reverse)=−f and tr(combined)=+f, with f=n/2−1 if n even else0. Permutation action on 3-subsets of the n−1 elementary squares twisted by the two sign characters has exactly the resulting character (N,−N,−f,f), and rational C2×C2 representations are determined by their four traces. Rational transfer gives quotient H5 ranks 0,(N−f)/2,(N+f)/2,0. Independently enumerated stable faces using explicit graph independent-four predicate and signed orbit contributions for n=4 through10: characters n4=(1,−1,−1,1), n5=(4,−4,0,0), n6=(10,−10,−2,2), up to n10=(84,−84,−4,4), all matching the formula.

value.rationale: The nonequivariant wedge rank already known does not tell how the two natural ladder involutions act; the exact full Klein-four character distinguishes reflection quotients and proves row swap kills all invariant rational classes. This is a motivated equivariant refinement for a standard grid-complex family, and its parity-dependent quotient ranks are useful even without an integral basis or an equivariant homotopy equivalence.
